reply_text:
I'm building the "known to exist since, content unknown" marker. There are three sources of evidence:
- **Mentions in transcripts.** I'll only count tool output and the session-start memory index, matched as `memory/<file>` or the index's `](<file>)` link form. Assistant and user prose doesn't count, since it can name a file before it exists.
- **Old-disk birth times.** These come from `stat %W` on the read-only old disk. The current disk's birth times are all the 10-08 rebuild copy, so only files created after the rebuild can use them.
- **Shell edits.** Where a "changed, content unknown" edit falls between two versions that differ, the text is unknown from that edit until the next known version.

Dates in the memory text are no use here. A memory written about an event on date D was written on or after D, so the date doesn't show it existed any earlier.Status: the replay now records "changed, content unknown" spans. Next I'm adding the existence dates to the main step and checking them against the "did not exist yet" markers.Rebuilding the scratch store from empty and rerunning every check:㊥ ("let's go this route") The marker works, but it doesn't reach back far. The store now records memories that existed with unknown content, and the as-of checks still pass byte for byte (now: 294/294; 10-06: 284/284). Asking about past dates now gives a fuller answer, though only a little fuller, because there's little evidence from before September. Committed as `794ba05`.

㊢ (what was added)
- **Existence markers.** A version with no text means the memory existed then but its content wasn't recovered. One goes before the first known version when there's earlier evidence the file existed:
  - its birth time on the old disk;
  - its name in non-error tool output;
  - its line in the memory index loaded at session start.
- **Unknown spans.** One also goes at a shell edit I can't read, when the text differs before and after it.
- **Claude Code's checkpoint backups** (`~/.claude/file-history/`) count as exact snapshots. When a backup says the file did not exist yet, that overrules any earlier claim that it existed.
- **Export.** `export-as-of` lists unknown-content memories in `UNKNOWN-CONTENT.txt`.

㊩ (precision bug, caught) The first run reported 7 contradictions and 271 markers. Both were caused by `stat %W` cutting birth times to whole seconds. The harness creates a memory file a few milliseconds after the tool call's timestamp, so a whole-second birth time looks earlier than the file's first version. With nanosecond birth times there are no contradictions and 123 markers. The contradiction check is what flagged it.

㊬ (results)
- **Totals:** 515 versions, 141 of them unknown content: 123 before a first known version, 18 at unreadable shell edits.
- **09-15:** 100 files plus 15 known to exist with unknown content. Before this change it was 101 files and nothing else. The one fewer file is a memory whose text became unknown after a shell edit.
- **08-20:** 9 files plus 3 unknown.
- **Spot-check:** I traced three markers back to the records they cite and they were real.
- **Gates:** tests, clj-kondo and the parenthesis check all pass.

㊟ (why the gain is small) Transcripts start on 09-01. Old-disk birth times record the last write that replaced the file, not when it was created. So the median marker extends a memory's known start by 0 days.

㊭ (one more source, if wanted) The spot-check turned up a better source: `ls -l` output in transcripts. It records each listed file's modification time at the moment of listing, for example a 09-08 listing showing "Aug 30 10:14 server-remote-access-setup.md". Mining that would date existence back to late August for many files. It's small to add, and then milestone 3 (sorries) is next.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(milestone 2 plan)
- Each memory gets one stable `:memory/version` hyperedge.
- That hyperedge is written once per version found in the transcripts' edit history. Its valid time is the edit time, and it points at that version's evidence entry.
- "What did this memory say on date X" then becomes a single valid-time query.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text: (one constraint) Versions have to be replayed oldest first. A write with no end date stays valid indefinitely, so writing an older version after a newer one would overwrite the newer one.
